_**Agent (composer-1.5)**_

Identifying the cause: react-grid-layout's `processGridItem` returns null for children without a key:

```javascript
if (!child || !child.key) return null;
```

Using `<>...</>` (React Fragment) as `gridContent` makes ReactGridLayout receive one child — the fragment. Fragments created with `<>` have no key, so `processGridItem` returns null and nothing renders.

Fix: pass an array of elements (each with a key) instead of a fragment:

_**Agent (composer-1.5)**_

Here’s what was going on:

**Cause:** `react-grid-layout`’s `processGridItem` ignores any child without a key:

```javascript
if (!child || !child.key) return null;
```

Using `<>...</>` (a React Fragment) makes ReactGridLayout receive a single child — the fragment. Fragments created with `<>` have no key, so `processGridItem` returns `null` and nothing is rendered.

**Fix:** Pass an array of elements instead of a fragment, so each grid item is a separate child with a key (`"a"`, `"b"`, `"c"`). ReactGridLayout can then match each child to its layout item and render them correctly.

**Note:** For sections like "Proyects", "Experience", and "Contact" that have no `layout` or `GridItems`, clicking them will set `gridLayout` and `gridContent` to `undefined`, which can cause ReactGridLayout to behave unexpectedly. Adding guards or default values for those sections would help.
